page: Microsoft Azure F16amds_v7 is a high-frequency compute and memory-dense virtual machine architecture running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 16-core, 16-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz with a single thread per core topology. The hardware configuration couples this compute foundation with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. The platform bundles 1,888 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and operates without discrete GPU accelerators. The CPU features extensive vector extensions, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware cryptography engines such as AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-threaded performance, with single-core stress-ng execution and bzip3 decompression testing in the top 10 percent of recorded results. Single-threaded gzip compression and lightweight machine learning inference also perform strongly, with small-parameter model generation reaching 420.78 tokens per second. Multi-threaded throughput, as measured by multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU metrics, settles into the middle performance tier. Memory subsystem testing reflects standard enterprise throughput, recording 108.05 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 68.96 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth across large memory blocks.

The inclusion of 1,888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage paired with dedicated non-hyperthreaded cores provides balanced resource density for latency-sensitive applications. Eliminating shared-thread contention offers predictable cycle allocation, although overall multi-threaded parallel throughput remains constrained by the 16-core envelope compared to higher core-count configurations. This hardware balance makes the instance appropriate for database workloads requiring rapid temporary scratch space, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, compression and decompression workflows, and analytical batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure F16amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring a dedicated 16-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. Designed for compute and data-intensive applications, the system provides 128.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-core allocation, and includes 1,888 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. The CPU supports AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core performance and decompression throughput, with balanced mid-tier results in multi-core metrics and uncached memory bandwidth. The architecture provides deterministic performance without thread contention, alongside high local disk throughput. Microsoft Azure F16amds_v7 is well suited for memory caching layers, local database hosting, compression processing, and moderate-scale model inference.
